label: 4th original token after an h/v-d/v-w/m style prefix (combinatorial n-gram detector)
explanation: Very sparse feature that fires only in the original phase, almost always at t=3 (76% of mass) or t=4 (22%), and never at the delimiter or during the copy phase. It is a conjunctive detector over the opening tokens: first token mostly h/v (or n), then d/v/k, then w/m, with the current input among 1/l/s/t (and less often m/r). The core pattern (h|v, d|v, w|m, then 1|l|s|t at t=3) has precision 1.0 on dev but covers only about 21% of activations. Widening each slot raises recall to about 42% but drops precision to about 48%. The rest are near-variants: the same pattern shifted by one step (e.g. n v w v [s]), or one slot outside the sets (e.g. l v w [1], x d d l [l]). Activation is fairly uniform (0.07-0.15). The strongest cases are h v d e [1] and v d m [1]. It does not fire on these tokens later in the sequence, or when the prefix tokens are absent. This looks like a direction in hidden-state space that only a specific mix of early tokens reaches, and a clean boolean predicate does not capture it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=h (+2.57), t=3 & prev_tok=m (+2.43), prev2_tok=d (+2.25), orig1=d (+2.11), prev3_tok=v (+2.03), prev2_tok=v (+1.81). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-2.14), prev3_tok=- (-1.66), n_digits=2 (-0.80), in_first=0 (-0.67).
